summary: One-time initializer for a custom memory pool allocator. Guarded by byte_7CD9C8 bit 0: on first call it allocates and zeroes a pool struct, allocates a pool descriptor holding a 32-entry array (count 32 stored in its first dword, each entry initialized through ThunkToFUN00491330), builds a linked list of pool-struct nodes, walks the entry array in 16-byte steps linking 12-byte free-list nodes, stores the pool pointer in dword_7CD9CC, constructs an allocator handle via ObjectConstructor_1710 into dword_7CD9D0, registers ResourceLinkedListTeardown as teardown callback, and returns a pointer to dword_7CD9CC. Called by Accessor (00490920) and GlobalDataRead (00490930).

operations.description: Skip the whole initialization when byte_7CD9C8 bit 0 is already set; otherwise set it to mark initialization in progress.
Allocate the 32-byte pool struct (eight dwords) via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper and zero all eight dwords.
Allocate the 4-byte pool descriptor via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper.
Allocate the 516-byte entry array via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper and store count 32 in its first dword.
Initialize the 32 pool entries by calling ThunkToFUN00491330 on each successive 4-byte slot of the array.
Store the entry array pointer into the pool descriptor (null if the allocation failed).
Allocate a 12-byte pool-struct node via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper.
Initialize the pool-struct node (pool pointer, next 0, flag 1) and link it into the pool struct's head/tail list, incrementing its node count.

Walk the entry array in 16-byte steps; for each entry allocate a 12-byte free-list node via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper, initialize it (entry pointer, next 0, flag 0), and link it into the free list, incrementing its count.
Store the pool struct pointer in global dword_7CD9CC (zero if the pool allocation failed).
Allocate the 4-byte handle storage and construct the allocator handle object via ObjectConstructor_1710 with argument 1; falls back to 0 when the allocation fails.
Store the allocator handle in global dword_7CD9D0.
Register ResourceLinkedListTeardown as a teardown callback via BooleanToIntConversion.
Return a pointer to the global pool descriptor dword_7CD9CC.

unresolved: The exact layouts of the pool struct and the free-list nodes are DERIVED from dword/byte indices in the raw body; not independently confirmed.
The semantics of the ObjectConstructor_1710 argument (1) and its return value are unknown.
When the descriptor allocation fails the decompiled body still dereferences the descriptor inside the walk loop; whether the original code carried a guard is not recoverable from this body.
What ThunkToFUN00491330 writes into each 32-byte entry and how the stored count is later consumed is unknown.
